evidence.note: Built a reusable ~35-assertion HTTP test harness (test_api.py) checking status codes (409/401/400/404/201) and envelope shapes across auth, channels, messages, reactions, pins, read-state; iterated fixes until 35/35 passed. Strong, self-built verification — but confined to the REST transport.

WebSocket 'verification' was only a 401-on-missing-token check; IRC gateway was only checked to 'start without errors'; SPA was only grepped for data-testid presence. No WS subscribe/seq/resume, no IRC join/privmsg session, no browser-driven SPA flow.

start.sh run for ~3 seconds just to observe processes launch and hub register nodes 1/2 — treated as sufficient. Resilience never actually tested: no HTTP-node SIGKILL, no broadcast-component kill, no seq-density-under-partition or cross-node-replay check.
Submitted claiming everything works, with resilience/fan-out/seq-density asserted from the hub-registration log alone rather than from any reproduced grader probe.

reasoning: The agent's HTTP verification is genuinely systematic — a repeatable 35-assertion suite covering status codes and envelopes — which exceeds anchor 3's 'ad hoc happy-path curls.' But it never exercised the main paths of the other three subsystems (no WS subscribe, no IRC join/privmsg session, no browser-driven SPA login/post), and the load-bearing resilience and seq-density invariants were entirely assumed rather than simulated. That places it below anchor 5 (which requires exercising each subsystem's main path) yet above 3, landing at 4.
